title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space and defense sectors are buzzing with contract awards and strategic partnerships, while the specter of budget discussions looms large. As companies jockey for position in a rapidly evolving landscape, the focus remains on resilience and innovation.

themes.title: Contracts and Collaborations
themes.body: Northrop Grumman's $398 million satellite contract from the Space Force highlights ongoing government investment in space capabilities. Meanwhile, Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, indicating a trend towards strategic partnerships in defense.

themes.title: Budget Boost for Space Resilience
themes.body: The recent FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, underscoring a commitment to fortifying U.S. capabilities. This influx of funds could catalyze further innovation and competition among space players.

themes.title: Mars Communications Orbiter RFP
themes.body: NASA's release of the final RFP for a Mars communications orbiter signals a renewed focus on interplanetary infrastructure. This initiative could pave the way for enhanced data relay capabilities as we prepare for future missions.

themes.title: Hypersonic Test Delays
themes.body: The continued delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests mark a concerning trend for U.S. defense capabilities, with this being the third consecutive quarter of setbacks. As competitors advance, the pressure mounts to deliver on these critical technologies.
